Hydrogen storage in natural gas pipelines, often referred to as line-pack storage, utilizes the existing network to store renewable energy by blending hydrogen with natural gas or storing pure hydrogen. This method offers significantly higher capacity than electrical grid storage, with the German natural gas network alone capable of storing over 200,000 GW·h (enough for several months) compared to only 40 GW·h for pumped storage, while experiencing minimal energy loss of <0.1%.

Blending hydrogen into existing infrastructure is technically feasible at concentrations typically between 5% and 20% by volume, which requires only modest modifications to monitoring and maintenance.
